A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central method and principal experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original planning and MBRL experiments, including Mountain Car, Dubins Car, Cartpole and MuJoCo results, plus appendix sensitivity analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds prediction-error experiments comparing directly learned temporally extended dynamics with iterated learned primitive dynamics in Appendix I.2.

M1.justification: The action-duration optimization, learned dynamics ensembles and UCB-based duration-range selection remain unchanged. New Algorithm 2 and expanded planning pseudocode document the existing framework; they do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: All original environments and control tasks remain. Appendix I.2 adds state-prediction evaluation under random primitive and randomly timed temporally extended action sequences in Cartpole, Ant and Half Cheetah, providing a limited additional test scenario within existing domains.

E2.justification: Table A7 adds an explicit comparison against iterating a learned primitive dynamics model to approximate temporally extended transitions. The original ASTD/PETS comparator and shared-versus-separate-model comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new prediction experiment uses random action sequences of length 500, state mean-squared error, and either minimum-duration actions or durations sampled uniformly between the stated bounds. These are additional evaluation protocols; existing environment settings and hyperparameter tables are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix I.2 adds a focused analysis of whether direct temporally extended prediction is more accurate than iterating a learned one-step model. Existing horizon sensitivity, discount-factor, failure-case and shared-versus-separate-model analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new prediction experiments disclose ten repetitions and report means, including a separate Ant mean after excluding four extreme runs. Existing five-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged; the PDFs do not indicate increased repetitions for earlier experiments.

E6.justification: Table A7 adds prediction-error results: the primitive model is better on primitive sequences, whereas direct temporally extended prediction is better on extended sequences. For example, Cartpole extended-sequence MSE is 0.0184 versus 0.065. Existing Tables 1–2 and A1–A6 and the earlier result plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: The return formulations, horizon arguments and comparison with Ni and Jang retain their mathematical substance. New Equations (5)–(6) spell out standard CEM mean and variance updates; the notation glossary and these implementation explanations introduce no substantive new theory or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about duration optimization, reduced planning complexity, faster MBRL and automatic duration-range selection. The new prediction experiment supports an existing claim rather than redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix I.2 interprets prediction errors through compounding model errors and hypothesizes that extreme Ant errors involve states outside the primitive model's training distribution. Section 5 also explicitly suggests fixed durations may suffice in Ant and Half Cheetah and acknowledges the overhead of flexible durations.

D1.justification: v2 adds training-loop pseudocode, explicit per-arm datasets, the log2(T) candidate-count specification, expanded ensemble-planning details and CEM update formulas. Its checklist provides a code-repository link. Existing architecture, hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain; these additions do not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds Auer et al. (2002) as the source for the UCB heuristic and explicitly identifies ASTD with PETS TS-infinity. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier temporal-abstraction approaches otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the method and experimental setup, expand the action-repeat discussion and reorganize ensemble-planning explanations. A notation glossary and NeurIPS checklist are added, with appendix reordering and renumbering. Most of the scientific narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table A7, a symbol table and Algorithm 2, and expands Algorithm A2. NeurIPS formatting changes typography, margins, display sizing and placement. Existing result figures and table structures are retained without substantive graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and reproducibility through explicit training and planning descriptions and a code-access pointer. Appendix I.2 supplies useful direct evidence for the existing prediction-error argument. The gain is limited: the diagnostic covers three existing environments, reports means without uncertainty, and leaves the cause of extreme Ant errors hypothetical. The principal results and conclusions remain unchanged.
